title: The project_not_registered hint names ward init where init cannot run; readBoundedFile has no O_NONBLOCK
description: Two items from the Opus review of ward-cli#267 (WCLI-140), both predating it and outside it. (1) The project_not_registered hint "Run ward init in a terminal to register this checkout" (src/contract/errors.ts) is also shown at a checkout where ward init fails with checkout_identity_unavailable (pruned worktree git directory, invalid nonce file, unwritable git directory): the same truthfulness question WCLI-140 L1 settled for the doctor report, on the error path. A new or reworded error needs an opum-doc ruling as an A/B draft. (2) readBoundedFile (src/adapters/checkout.ts) opens without O_NONBLOCK, so a FIFO swapped in between the lstat and the open could block the read. It needs a same-account attacker, outside ADR 0002, so treat it as hardening only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The project_not_registered hint no longer sends the developer to ward init where init cannot run, as ruled by opum-doc
readBoundedFile cannot block on a swapped-in FIFO, or the item is closed as accepted residual with a note

implementationNotes: Item 2 (readBoundedFile) implemented on fix/WCLI-144-hint-and-nonblock, local only, not pushed, waiting on the opum-doc ruling for item 1 so the task stays one PR. readBoundedFile now opens O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and refuses a descriptor that is not a regular file; it is exported so a test can reach it. Test: a child process (killed at 5s, so a regression fails rather than hangs) reads a regular file as the control, and a FIFO with no writer, expecting an undefined read at once. Controls: removing O_NONBLOCK makes the FIFO test fail at 5.0s; removing only the fstat isFile guard does NOT turn it red on this platform (the non-blocking read of a writerless FIFO already throws), so the guard is defence in depth that no test pins. Item 1 (the project_not_registered hint) is an A/B sent to the leader: A reword one static hint to point at checkout_identity_unavailable first (recommended), B choose hint or error by an identityBindable probe at each raise site.

Item 1 implemented per DEC-255 (a11), option A (opum-doc ruling relayed by the leader; record opum-ai/opum-doc#1616): the project_not_registered hint stays one static string and now reads "Run `ward init` in a terminal to register this checkout. If init reports that it could not give the checkout an identity, fix what that error names first; init cannot register the checkout until then." The message is unchanged; option B (probing identityBindable at every raise site) was rejected. Pinned by an exact-string test in test/checkout-identity.test.ts. One PR with item 2 (readBoundedFile, noted earlier).

REVIEW VERDICT round 1 (a DEC-183 reviewer unit, model claude-opus-5-5, a model unit and not a human reviewer), relayed verbatim by the leader, for ward-cli#276 at head be9514ec63c0dc9e9efd57c68468897699e3c9af: APPROVE. Verdict file 6201 bytes, sha256 63a04186717134c13d7c925decf6a43dea73c0127e740c4e271ba7175c22e320. Held until DEC-255 (a11) reached opum-doc main (6434767, opum-ai/opum-doc#1617), then merged as squash 272b13f516ae8f24742abef265101493c87b9185 with Check, Docs and Tracker integrity green on that head. FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE, nothing filed: (1) the 5000 ms child kill in the readBoundedFile test ties bun's per-test timeout; (2) the fstat isFile guard is unpinned, and /dev/null would pin it cheaply (pread returns 0, so the function would return an empty string without the guard); (3) new URL().pathname should be fileURLToPath.

VERDICT: APPROVE
opum-ai/ward-cli#276 (WCLI-144), head be9514ec63c0dc9e9efd57c68468897699e3c9af, read-only tree review. No BLOCKING findings; 3 LOW.

ITEM 1 (hint):
- src/contract/errors.ts:258: I compared the hint with the DEC-255 (a11) string character by character, and it matches exactly, including both backticks around `ward init`, the period after "checkout", the comma after "identity", the semicolon after "first" and the final period. The message at :256-257 is unchanged. That one line is the only change to errors.ts.
- The pointer resolves: "could not give the checkout an identity" matches the checkout_identity_unavailable message at errors.ts:200 ("Ward could not give this checkout an identity…").
- test/checkout-identity.test.ts:575-585 pins both the hint and the message with toBe. No doc, skill or other test carries the old hint text (grep over the whole tree, .quest excluded). binding_requires_terminal's similar hint at :246 is a different error and is untouched, which is correct.

ITEM 2 (readBoundedFile, src/adapters/checkout.ts:89-111):
- Regular files: O_NONBLOCK has no effect on a regular file's open or pread. The single readSync at position 0 and the maxBytes+1 bound are byte-identical to before.
- fd always closed: the guard's early `return undefined` at :101 is inside the try, so the finally at :109 closes the descriptor. Open failures leave descriptor undefined and skip the close.
- Link semantics are unchanged: O_NOFOLLOW was already present, so a link at the path still fails the open (ELOOP), and the result is undefined as before. Both callers already lstat-require isFile before calling (gitDirectoryOf :116-118, readCheckoutId :150). fstat on the opened fd therefore enforces exactly what the callers already expect, at the right moment (after open). No legitimate input changes behaviour.
- Callers on undefined: gitDirectoryOf returns undefined, then bindCheckoutIdentity throws checkout_identity_unavailable. readCheckoutId returns undefined, then the O_EXCL create hits EEXIST on the planted FIFO, the re-read is undefined, and it throws checkout_identity_unavailable. So there is no hang and no overwrite, and locateCheckout just reports no checkoutId.
- AC index 1 ("cannot block on a swapped-in FIFO") is met by O_NONBLOCK, and the FIFO test pins that. The guard is not required by the AC.
- Exporting readBoundedFile for the test is acceptable. It lives in an internal adapter module, there is no library surface, and the export changes no behaviour.

LOW findings:
1. LOW test/checkout-identity.test.ts:550: the child kill timer (5000 ms) equals Bun's default per-test timeout. CI runs plain `bun test` via `bun run check` (package.json:25), and there is no --timeout or bunfig timeout. Bun's timer starts first, so a regression goes red as a test timeout rather than the {exitCode,out} mismatch. That is still red, consistent with "fails at 5.0 s". However, `child.exited` is then abandoned. If the run ends before the 5000 ms setTimeout fires (the next test is synchronous, and this may be the last file), a child blocked in open() is orphaned. Fix: kill well under the test timeout (for example 2000 ms), or give the two tests an explicit timeout above the kill deadline.
2. LOW test/checkout-identity.test.ts:541-584 (no case pins the guard): the fstat isFile guard at checkout.ts:101 is unpinned, as the writer said. Their stated reason is probably imprecise. readSync with a numeric position is a pread, and pread on any pipe fails ESPIPE, with or without a writer, so a FIFO can never discriminate the guard. A directory can't either: pread gives EISDIR and the catch returns undefined. /dev/null should discriminate cheaply and in-process, with no child needed. Without the guard, pread returns 0 and the function returns ""; with it, the function returns undefined. Suggest adding `expect(readBoundedFile("/dev/null", 64)).toBeUndefined()`, then mutating the check (drop the guard) and confirming it goes red on both macOS and the linux-arm64 runner. A pread on a char device that threw on some platform would silently stop the case discriminating. This is optional, and AC 1 is met without it.
3. LOW test/checkout-identity.test.ts:536-537: `new URL(...).pathname` percent-encodes spaces and other reserved characters in the checkout path. `fileURLToPath(new URL(...))` is robust. It is harmless on current paths.

Also checked, no finding:
- Child-process test: bounded (kill plus test timeout). Temp files go under `root` (mkdtemp in tmpdir), which afterAll removes with rmSync recursive, FIFO included. A writerless open O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK of a FIFO succeeds immediately on both Linux and macOS (POSIX), and fstat refuses it, so the outcome is deterministic on both. Output is tiny, so reading stdout after exit cannot deadlock on the pipe buffer.
- Docs: no ADR lists a FIFO-in-readBoundedFile residual that would now be stale. ADR 0026's residual (docs/adr/0026…:98) is the write-side link swap, which is unchanged. The ADR 0006:78 FIFO line concerns backup restore and is unrelated.
- DEC-182 (1) fence class: none. The four files are the tracker record, the named checkout-identity adapter, the error catalog string and a test. No CI, deps/lockfile, settings, hooks, build, or auth/credential paths are touched.

COULD NOT VERIFY (tree read only, no shell):
- CI results for Check, Docs and Tracker integrity on this SHA.
- The writer's two mutation controls (no O_NONBLOCK → red at 5.0 s; no guard → still green).
- That mkfifo is present on the linux-arm64 runner image.
- Bun's readSync-with-position → pread mapping, and /dev/null pread behaviour on both platforms (my LOW 2 reasoning rests on both).
- The full transitive import graph of the child. I traced it as far as checkout.ts → project-files, errors, vault-state (→ identifiers, profile, secret); only src/cli/guard.ts and src/adapters/keychain.ts mention keyring. The child runs outside the keychain mock, but it calls only readBoundedFile.
- That the .quest/tasks/WCLI-144.json change was written by quest rather than by hand. The status is In Progress, both ACs are unchecked (expected before close), and the implementation notes match the code.
finalSummary: Item 1: the project_not_registered hint is the DEC-255 (a11) option A string, pinned by an exact-string test. Item 2: readBoundedFile opens O_NONBLOCK and refuses a non-regular file. Both landed in ward-cli#276 (squash 272b13f) after an Opus-model APPROVE recorded verbatim in the notes. Three test-hardening LOWs are noted as a follow-up candidate, not filed.
